title: Linkability of repeated telemetry to the same wearer
description: Continuous capture of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps allows the wearable device to associate multiple observations over time with the same wearer, enabling construction of a persistent activity trail even if direct identifiers are absent.
assumptions: The device or its software stores or processes telemetry over time under a stable device/user context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent observations; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Identifiability of the wearer from telemetry patterns
description: GPS traces, timestamps, heart-rate patterns, and activity data can uniquely distinguish or re-identify the wearer, especially when combined with home/work locations or habitual routines inferred from the data.
assumptions: Telemetry is sufficiently granular to reveal distinctive movement or behavioral patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from quasi-identifiers/inferred uniqueness; exact node id may differ in some LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location information
description: The flow contains sensitive personal data, including physiological measurements and precise location with timestamps. If exposed within the device context, this can reveal health status, routines, visits to sensitive places, and daily habits.
assumptions: Telemetry is accessible to device software components, storage, logs, or interfaces beyond the minimum necessary scope.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure of sensitive personal data; exact subtree label may vary.

title: Unawareness of continuous sensing scope
description: The wearer may be insufficiently aware that the device continuously captures multiple sensor streams, including GPS and timestamps, and may not understand the granularity, persistence, or implications of this collection.
assumptions: The device UX does not clearly and continuously communicate active sensing and data categories being collected.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency about collection; exact node id may vary.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive or unjustified data collection
description: Continuous collection of heart rate, steps, GPS position, and timestamps may exceed what is necessary for a given purpose if all elements are captured by default, creating risk of violating data minimization, purpose limitation, or consent requirements.
assumptions: Not all collected fields are strictly necessary for the stated functionality, or valid consent/notice is incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to over-collection and insufficient legal basis; exact node id may differ.

title: Stable device identifier enables linkage of activity batches over time
description: The wearable sends a device id together with exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps. A stable identifier allows the companion app, or parties with access to synced data, to link multiple uploads to the same person/device across time and potentially across contexts.
assumptions: The device id is persistent across syncs and visible to the app or backend components reachable through the app.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether linkage is modeled as linkability of messages or records.

title: Sensor batches reveal sensitive inferences about the user
description: Exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps can reveal home/work locations, routines, health status, religious attendance, social relationships, and other sensitive attributes when analyzed by the companion app.
assumptions: The app stores, processes, or exposes raw or derived location/activity data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for inference from observed data.

title: Identity disclosure through direct and quasi-identifiers in synced data
description: The combination of device id, precise GPS traces, and timestamps can directly identify or single out the user, especially by revealing recurring locations such as home and workplace.
assumptions: The app can associate device ids or location patterns with a real-world individual.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact subtree may differ depending on whether disclosure is treated as identification from identifiers or from data combination.

title: Excessive disclosure of precise location and activity details to the app
description: Syncing full GPS traces, detailed exercise sessions, exact timestamps, and device id may disclose more personal data than necessary for core companion-app functionality, increasing privacy exposure.
assumptions: Some app features could operate with reduced precision, aggregation, or fewer attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data minimization / unnecessary disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Users may be unaware of the scope and granularity of synced data
description: Users may not understand that the wearable sync includes precise GPS traces, timestamps, and persistent device identifiers, nor the resulting profiling and retention implications within the companion app.
assumptions: The app's notices or UI do not clearly explain the categories, precision, frequency, and downstream uses of synced data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency.

title: Sync may occur without valid, specific consent or another appropriate legal basis
description: Collecting and importing detailed exercise and location histories from the wearable into the companion app may require explicit, granular consent or another valid legal basis. If sync is enabled by default or bundled, processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable law/policy requires a legal basis and potentially heightened protection for location or health-related data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for consent/legal-basis non-compliance; exact node id may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Insufficient proof of user consent or sync choices
description: If the app cannot demonstrate when and how the user enabled syncing of exercise sessions and GPS traces, the user may later plausibly deny having agreed to this collection or transfer, creating accountability and dispute issues.
assumptions: The system relies on user choice for enabling sync and does not maintain robust consent/audit records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation of consent/action rather than message transmission itself.

title: Inference of health status and lifestyle from logged meals and weight
description: Calorie intake, meal details, and weight entries can reveal sensitive health information such as dieting behavior, obesity risk, eating patterns, pregnancy, religious practices, or medical conditions. Anyone with access to the app-side data flow or stored inputs may infer more than the user intended to disclose.
assumptions: The companion app processes or stores the submitted entries in a way accessible to internal components, operators, or attackers beyond the immediate input interaction.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort; I am confident about the inference threat but less certain of the exact LINDDUN Pro subtree numbering without reference material.

title: Linkability of repeated nutrition and weight logs to the same individual
description: Repeated manual entries over time can be linked together to build a longitudinal profile of the wearer, connecting meal habits, calorie intake, and weight changes to the same person. This enables tracking of routines and correlations with other app or device data.
assumptions: The app associates entries with a persistent account, device identifier, or session.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability is strong; exact node id is approximate.

title: Identifiability of the wearer through uniquely identifying diet and weight patterns
description: Even if explicit identifiers are minimized, combinations of meal timing, unusual foods, calorie patterns, and weight trajectories may uniquely identify the wearer when combined with auxiliary information.
assumptions: An observer has access to the submitted data and some external background knowledge.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; identifiability clearly applies.

title: Lack of evidence about who entered or modified nutrition and weight data
description: If the app does not maintain trustworthy records of entry creation and modification, the wearer may later deny having entered certain meals or weight values, or another person using the device could repudiate the action. This can affect accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: The app allows local access by multiple people or lacks strong authentication, timestamps, or integrity-protected audit trails.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort.

title: Disclosure of sensitive dietary and weight data during entry handling
description: The flow contains highly sensitive personal data. If the app exposes entries through insecure local storage, logs, screenshots, clipboard use, debugging interfaces, or transmission protections that are insufficient after capture, unauthorized parties could learn the user's meals, calorie intake, and weight.
assumptions: The app or surrounding platform may retain or expose entered values beyond the immediate UI interaction.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; disclosure threat strongly applies.

title: Insufficient user awareness about collection and downstream use of nutrition and weight entries
description: The wearer may not understand how detailed meal, calorie, and weight logs will be used, retained, combined with other wellness data, or shared with service providers. This undermines informed participation and meaningful control.
assumptions: The app's notices, just-in-time explanations, or settings are incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate.

title: Collection of calorie, meal, and weight data without valid consent or appropriate legal basis
description: Because these entries can constitute health-related or otherwise sensitive personal data, collecting and processing them without explicit, specific, and informed consent or another valid legal basis may violate privacy requirements.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy treats these data as sensitive and requires heightened protections.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate and depends on jurisdiction, but non-compliance risk is plausible.

title: Sensitive health logs can be inferred from stored records
description: The health log store contains detailed calorie intake, weight history, and exercise session records. Access to these records, or even derived metadata from them, can reveal sensitive health conditions, lifestyle patterns, dieting behavior, pregnancy indicators, eating disorders, or other intimate attributes about the user.
assumptions: The datastore persists logs in a form accessible to internal services, administrators, backups, analytics pipelines, or attackers who gain access.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for inference from stored content may vary.

title: Health log entries enable linkage across sessions and datasets
description: Repeated writes of health logs tied to the same app account or device can allow records over time to be linked together, building a longitudinal profile of the user's habits, body metrics, and routines. If combined with other datasets, this may also link the user across contexts.
assumptions: Records are stored with stable identifiers such as account ID, device ID, or persistent pseudonyms.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact linkage subtree may differ depending on whether linkage is via identifiers, metadata, or content similarity.

title: Stored health logs may disclose sensitive personal information
description: The datastore holds explicit personal data about calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions. Unauthorized access, overly broad internal access, insecure backups, or secondary use of the store could disclose highly sensitive health and lifestyle information.
assumptions: The store may be reachable by multiple components or personnel, and stored data may be retained in backups or replicas.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact disclosure subtree depends on the specific disclosure vector.

title: Users may be unaware of the extent and retention of stored health logs
description: When the app writes detailed health logs to the datastore, users may not realize how much detail is stored, how long it is retained, whether historical versions persist, or which parties and subsystems can access it. This reduces users' awareness of privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: The app or service may not clearly communicate storage scope, retention, backup practices, or downstream access.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact detectability subtree may differ because this concerns lack of user awareness of storage/retention practices.

title: Health logs may be used for purposes beyond user-expected tracking
description: Data written for personal health tracking could later be used for analytics, profiling, recommendations, advertising, insurance-related assessment, or model training in ways not expected by the user. Such secondary use can make the processing non-compliant with user expectations and intended purpose limitation.
assumptions: The organization may reuse stored logs for secondary purposes beyond core logging and retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for content unawareness or unexpected secondary use may vary.

title: Storing detailed health logs may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention requirements
description: Persisting calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions in detailed or long-lived form may exceed what is necessary for the service, especially if raw logs are retained indefinitely, replicated broadly, or reused for unrelated purposes. This creates risk of non-compliance with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements impose constraints on necessity, retention, access control, transparency, or lawful basis for processing health-related data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact non-compliance subtree depends on the governing requirement (e.g., minimization, retention, transparency, lawful basis).

title: Stored location traces enable linkage of records to the same individual over time
description: GPS traces with timestamps written by the mobile app can be linked across sessions and days, allowing records in the location history store to be associated with the same person or device and correlated with other datasets.
assumptions: The store retains identifiers, stable pseudonyms, account references, device identifiers, or otherwise preserves continuity between writes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on common LINDDUN Pro linkage threats for persistent records; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Location history can identify a person through unique mobility patterns
description: Even if explicit identifiers are absent, fine-grained GPS traces with timestamps are often highly unique and can reveal home/work locations or habitual routes, enabling identification of the data subject.
assumptions: The stored traces are sufficiently granular and retained long enough to infer recurring patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from stored data; exact numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro editions.

title: Sensitive location history may be disclosed from the data store
description: The location history store contains highly sensitive GPS traces and timestamps. Unauthorized access, overbroad internal access, or secondary use could disclose visits, routines, and presence at sensitive places.
assumptions: The store is accessible to administrators, services, analysts, or third parties beyond the minimum necessary scope.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for stored personal data; exact subnode may vary.

title: Stored traces allow detection of presence, absence, and routines
description: By analyzing timestamps and coordinates in the location history store, an observer can detect when the user was at home, away, commuting, or visiting specific places, exposing behavioral patterns and current or past presence.

uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability from stored observations; exact numbering may differ.

title: Collection and retention of location history may exceed user expectations or legal basis

assumptions: The system stores precise location history beyond what is strictly necessary or without clearly communicated controls.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for non-compliance related to collection/retention of personal data.

title: App may be unable to prove or contest user consent for location-history writes
description: If the mobile app writes GPS traces to the store without robust consent records or audit evidence, the user may later deny having agreed to persistent location-history collection, or the controller may be unable to demonstrate lawful authorization.
assumptions: Consent or another lawful basis is required and evidence of that basis is not strongly bound to each write operation.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation in privacy contexts is less commonly modeled for this flow; node id is an approximate best fit.

title: Users may be unaware that precise location traces are persistently stored
description: The flow writes GPS traces with timestamps into a location history store, which may not be obvious to users if notices, indicators, or controls are unclear. This undermines users' awareness of collection, retention, and downstream use.
assumptions: The app UX does not clearly communicate persistent storage and retention of location history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact subnode numbering may vary by version.

title: Cross-session health logs enable linkage of records to the same individual
description: The analytics service reads calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions from the health log store. Even if individual entries were collected at different times, stable identifiers, account references, device identifiers, or consistent behavioral patterns can allow records to be linked together and tied to one person over time.
assumptions: The store or query context contains a persistent identifier, pseudonym, or sufficiently distinctive combination of attributes to correlate entries across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers/correlation across sessions.

title: Health-condition analysis can infer sensitive medical attributes
description: By reading longitudinal calorie, weight, and exercise logs, the analytics service may infer sensitive health conditions, risks, or lifestyle patterns beyond what was explicitly provided in each log entry. Such inference can reveal special-category personal data.

uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture inference of sensitive attributes from observed data.

title: Analytics service can detect presence and activity patterns of a user
description: Repeated reads of health logs across sessions can reveal whether a specific user exists in the dataset, when they were active, and how frequently they log calorie, weight, or exercise data. This exposes observability of participation and behavior.
assumptions: The service can query or access user-scoped records and timestamps or similar metadata.

title: Broad longitudinal access exceeds data minimization for health analysis
description: Reading calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions may involve collecting more historical detail, granularity, or categories of data than are necessary for the stated health-condition analysis. Excessive retention or unrestricted querying increases disclosure impact if misused or breached.
assumptions: The analysis objective could be achieved with less data, aggregation, shorter time windows, or fewer attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture disclosure through unnecessary or overly broad data access.

title: Secondary analytics use may be unclear to the individual
description: Individuals may not understand that logs entered for tracking diet, weight, or exercise are later read across sessions for health-condition analysis. If this downstream use is not transparent, users may be unaware of the scope and implications of processing.
assumptions: Notices or UI explanations do not clearly describe longitudinal health-condition analysis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Processing of longitudinal health logs may lack a valid legal basis or exceed stated purpose
description: Health-condition analysis on calorie, weight, and exercise logs involves sensitive personal data and potentially profiling. If the analytics service processes these logs without an appropriate legal basis, explicit consent where required, or within a purpose compatible with collection, the flow may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy treats inferred or explicit health data as regulated sensitive data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture non-compliance with legal basis, purpose limitation, or special-category data requirements.

title: Cross-session location history enables linkage of records to the same individual
description: The analytics query uses location history across sessions, allowing records from multiple sessions to be linked together into a single longitudinal profile of one person's movements and routines. Even if session-level identifiers were intended to be separate, the datastore-to-analytics flow supports correlation over time.
assumptions: DS2 stores persistent or quasi-persistent identifiers, timestamps, or stable trajectory features that let P3 associate multiple sessions with the same person.

assumptions: P3 computes or can access fine-grained location/time sequences sufficient to infer unique patterns such as home and workplace.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability from data content/inference; exact subtree label may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

description: By querying location history across sessions, the service can infer private facts such as religious attendance, medical visits, political participation, intimate relationships, or other sensitive behavioral patterns from repeated visits and trajectories.

title: Secondary use of location history for behavioral profiling may be unexpected
description: Users may have provided location data for operational features, but querying it across sessions to derive daily routine and movement patterns constitutes profiling and a broader use that may not be expected or understood by the data subject.
assumptions: The original purpose presented to users did not clearly include longitudinal behavioral analytics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unexpected secondary use/purpose expansion; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

description: Using stored location history across sessions for routine and movement-pattern analysis may be incompatible with the consent obtained or with data minimization and purpose-limitation obligations, especially if retention and profiling were not explicitly justified.
assumptions: Consent, notice, or policy constraints do not explicitly authorize cross-session routine analysis, or retention is broader than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance related to consent/purpose limitation/retention; exact subtree numbering may differ.

assumptions: The flow may traverse networks or components where transport security, endpoint hardening, or log minimization could be insufficient.

Because the content concerns health-condition risks and behavioral trends, disclosure could be especially harmful.
assumptions: The app may cache or display returned insights and the device may be shared, compromised, or insufficiently protected.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for endpoint-side disclosure/storage exposure; exact subtree naming may differ.

title: Returned analytics enable linkage across sessions or contexts
